transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah… I guess what brings me in is that I’m getting really scared by what happens when I’m by myself at night. Like, after everything’s quiet and I’m alone, if I start eating, it doesn’t feel like a normal choice anymore. It’s like something flips or takes over, and even while I’m literally thinking, “Stop, put the food away, you don’t need this,” I just… don’t stop.

I know that sounds kind of dramatic, but that’s how it feels. I’ll be standing there or sitting there with food, and part of me is watching it happen and telling myself to stop, and another part is just going. It’s not even enjoyable after a point. It’s more like I’m on autopilot, and I can’t get control back once it starts. That’s the part that made me think I probably need help, because it keeps feeling bigger than just “bad habits” or not having enough willpower.
After these episodes of eating, do you ever try to compensate by making yourself sick, using laxatives, exercising a lot, or doing something else to try to 'undo' the eating?

Yeah… I do. I mean, that’s the part I feel most ashamed saying out loud, but yes. After I eat like that, I usually end up going to the bathroom and making myself throw up.

It’s not like I’m proud of it, or like it feels like some calm, planned thing. It’s more like once I realize how much I’ve eaten, I get this panic in my head about the calories and what it’s going to do to my body, and I start thinking I have to get it out before it “counts” or before it settles in. I know that probably doesn’t make sense medically, but in the moment it feels like the only way to undo what just happened. Like if I don’t do it, I’ll be stuck with it, and I can’t tolerate that feeling.

Sometimes I’ll sit there for a few minutes trying to talk myself out of it, but then the anxiety gets so loud that I just… go and do it. It’s really embarrassing to admit.
